investment_policy_en:
The managers seek to differentiate between structural winners and losers. The long positions of the fund are focused on dominant franchises with under-levered balance sheets, positioned to take advantage of structural growth opportunities. The team also makes use of additional investment techniques such as shorting to capitalise on the weakest companies most exposed to competitive threats and financial distress, as well as options to capture additional alpha and manage portfolio risk.

In the short book, the team looks for companies that are the mirror image of the long positions, or those with a deteriorating fundamental outlook and several red flags around their balance sheets. The portfolio is run in an unconstrained manner and represents a high conviction portfolio of our very best ideas from across emerging markets. The fund maintains higher levels of active share versus a long-only equivalent and equity market exposure typically around 100-110% of fund TNA under normal market conditions.

The fund aims to achieve capital growth over the long term.

The fund invests at least 70% of its assets in equities of companies that are listed, headquartered or do most of their business in global emerging markets including Latin America, Asia, Africa, Eastern Europe (including Russia) and the Middle East. The fund may also invest up to 20% of its assets in money market instruments on an ancillary basis. The fund may invest less than 50% of its assets (directly and/or indirectly) in China A and B shares (in aggregate).
